source: Sections 3.1-3.5 and 4 of the attribution page. Run counts restate 3.1 (one run per signal, repeated after each risk-target update), 3.2 (v(N) and v(N without k)) and 3.4 (2^K coalition values, 2^K - 1 backtests; sampled orders or signal families with many signals), as in i3. Sums restate 3.1 (residual kept as a separate term), 3.2 (contributions need not sum), 3.3 (Eq. 9; constraint portfolios, Eq. 17; dynamic model with constraints on the next trade only, an approximation, p. 7; combinatorial and non-convex constraints outside the treatment, pp. 7, 14), 3.4 (shares sum to v(N) of the coalition game) and 4.2 (shares sum to v(N) - v(empty set) of the chosen value). Ids are the headings' slugs.

questions.label: Question 1
questions.text: Is the policy a known convex optimiser with a quadratic risk or cost term whose optimality equations are available?

questions.label: Question 2
questions.text: Can we rerun the policy with signals removed?

link.text: rules, black boxes, learned policies; round lots or a minimum trade size

policies.title: Static optimiser
policies.text: quadratic risk or cost term, convex constraints
policies.detail: The split is read from the optimality equations at the joint optimum. Durin's split needs no rerun, and the signal positions sum to the actual position. Grinold–Easton also needs no rerun. It keeps each binding constraint as a separate portfolio.

policies.title: Dynamic optimiser
policies.text: Gârleanu–Pedersen: each signal's forecast decays at its own rate
policies.detail: Durin's recursion applies with modified forecasts and matrices, without a rerun. Durin imposes constraints on the next trade only and keeps the unconstrained value function. With constraints, this treatment is an approximation.

policies.title: Optimiser with round lots or a minimum trade size
policies.text: combinatorial or non-convex constraints: outside Durin's treatment
policies.detail: These constraints are combinatorial or non-convex, so Durin's treatment does not apply. If the optimiser can be rerun with signals removed, stand-alone proxies, leave-one-out or coalition Shapley apply.

policies.title: Rule, black box or learned policy
policies.detail: The policy supplies no optimality equations. If it can be rerun with signals removed, stand-alone proxies, leave-one-out or coalition Shapley apply. Section 5.3 proposes later work on learned policies.

policies.title: Policy we cannot rerun
policies.text: only the P&L record and the indicators
policies.detail: Only the P&L record and the indicators remain. Statistical attribution gives shares of a model's prediction or of explained variance, not of realised P&L. Section 5.3 proposes a surrogate route.

methods.title: Durin (2014)
methods.text: one set of effective matrices *!{Q}_{t}*, *!{P}_{t}* for every signal, from the multipliers at the joint optimum

methods.title: Grinold–Easton
methods.text: each binding constraint is a separate source with its own portfolio
methods.sum: exact, with one portfolio per constraint

methods.title: Durin, dynamic model
methods.text: modified forecasts and matrices; constraints on the next trade only

methods.title: Stand-alone proxies
methods.text: one signal at a time, own risk target; NNLS fit, iterated on the targets

methods.title: Leave-one-out
methods.sum: need not sum to the total

methods.title: Coalition Shapley
methods.text: marginal contributions averaged over coalitions; with many signals, sampled orders or signal families
methods.runs: 2*^{K}* coalition values, or a sampled budget

methods.title: Statistical attribution
methods.text: shares of a model's prediction or of explained variance: Shapley *R*^{2}, SHAP, SAGE
methods.runs: none: model fits on the record
methods.sum: the chosen value, not realised P&L
